lines.text: How many triangles have sides growing by the same multiplier?
lines.caption: How many triangles have sides growing by the same multiplier?

lines.text: The triangle has three different whole sides, each the last one times a fixed multiplier.
lines.caption: The triangle has three different whole sides, each the last one times a fixed multiplier.

lines.text: The longest is two thousand twenty-five. How many triangles?
lines.caption: The longest is two thousand twenty-five. How many triangles?

lines.text: The sides always look like k squared, forty-five k, and two thousand twenty-five.
lines.caption: The sides always look like k squared, forty-five k, and two thousand twenty-five.

lines.text: Here k runs from one to forty-four. Which ones close into a triangle?
lines.caption: Here k runs from one to forty-four. Which ones close into a triangle?

lines.text: The short sides must add up to more than the longest. At twenty-seven, they fall short.
lines.caption: The short sides must add up to more than the longest. At twenty-seven, they fall short.

lines.text: At twenty-eight, they just make it. And so does every bigger one!
lines.caption: At twenty-eight, they just make it. And so does every bigger one!

lines.text: Twenty-eight up to forty-four. That's seventeen triangles!
lines.caption: Twenty-eight up to forty-four. That's seventeen triangles!

lines.text: Why those sides? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
